# Success

Authors will be able to describe and check existing tutorials without changing tools. The registry will help learners choose materials suited to their goals and experience, and help instructors assess lessons for reuse. Both will see the requirements, check results, and review status in a common format across engines.

The table compares documented results with grant-end targets. We will update the baseline at grant start to include any completed pilot work.

| Measure | Documented baseline | Grant-end target |
|--------------------------------|-------------------|--------------------------------|
| Adapters with capability reports | 0 demonstrated | 3 initial adapters |
| Tutorials indexed through tutorialverse | 0 demonstrated | 5–10 across supported formats |
| External reviewers of schema, adapters, or tutorials | 0 documented reviews | At least 3 |
| Example tutorials tested in CI | 0 demonstrated | 4, collectively covering all adapters |
| Integration templates | 0 demonstrated | 3–4 |
| Reusable tutorial-validation workflow | 0 demonstrated | At least 1 |

Completion requires version 1.0 of the schema, R package, and registry. The pilot must also test published review and governance policies, including procedures for handling stale resources.

Validation will apply only to the checks reported for each engine and environment. During the grant, we will track external submissions and review participation, and measure the effort authors spend supplying missing metadata. After release, we will use outdated check results and broken links to prioritize maintenance, and package coverage to identify gaps in the registry.

Future work could add adapters for other tutorial engines or connect the registry to pkgdown, R-universe, and educational catalogs. Multilingual metadata, richer accessibility checks, and instructor collections remain outside the initial funded scope.
